docs.title: Query Builder
docs.text: ZubZet now includes a Query Builder based on CakePHP\Database. This provides a more intuitive and powerful way to create and manage complex MySQL queries.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
Alongside the existing file-internal routing system (controller-based actions), ZubZet now also provides a flexible route definition system.

This new approach allows you to explicitly declare routes, assign them to specific HTTP methods (GET, POST, …), and forward them to controller actions. It makes routing more organized, supports route grouping, and gives you greater control over your application’s structure.

docs.title: ZubZet Core
docs.text: 1. Localization System The currently implemented localization system in ZubZet is considered deprecated. While it has served its purpose for handling multiple languages and regional variations, its architecture no longer meets the evolving requirements of the platform. As a result, it will soon be replaced with a more efficient, flexible, and maintainable solution that better aligns with future development goals and user needs.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
For better project organization, several structural changes have been introduced:

  • All developer-related files (z_controllers, z_models, z_views, z_database, …) have been moved to the app/ directory. This keeps the application logic and internal code well-structured and separated from public-facing resources.

  • A new webroot/ directory has been added to contain all public files. Any files that should be publicly accessible (e.g. assets like images, CSS, or JavaScript) should be placed here. In contrast, private files such as configurations and settings remain in the project’s root directory, ensuring they are not exposed.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text:
1. Move the following folders: 

    - z_controllers   → app/Controllers
- z_models        → app/Models
- z_views         → app/Views
- z_database      → app/Database
- routes          → app/Routes

  2. In package.json, rename: package.json change 

    - z_database/import.php
+ app/Database/import.php

  3. Create a new folder called webroot.

  4. Delete the existing .htaccess file. Then create a new .htaccess file inside webroot: .htaccess 

    RewriteEngine On 
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f 
RewriteRule . index.php [L,QSA]

  5. Move everything that should be publicly accessible into webroot (e.g. assets/).

  6. Create a new index.php inside webroot: index.php 

    <?php

    // -----------------------------
    // Do not change this file as it is the entrypoint for web requests.
    // -----------------------------

    chdir(__DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . '..' . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR);

    // Try multiple locations for the entry scripts
    $entryScripts = [
        "index.php",
        "zubzet.php",
        "zubzet",
    ];

    $entryScriptFound = false;

    foreach($entryScripts as $entryScript) {
        if(!file_exists($entryScript)) break;

        require_once $entryScript;
        $entryScriptFound = true;
    }

    // If no entry script is found, return a 500 error
    if(!$entryScriptFound) {
        http_response_code(500);
        echo "No entry script found.";
        exit(1);
    }

?>

  7. Run the following command to require the desired version and update your composer.json accordingly: 

    composer require zubzet/framework:1.0.0

  8. Then, update the package to make sure all dependencies are resolved correctly: 

    composer update zubzet/frameworkDatums

Upgrade script for Linux The script must be in the root directory, and the project inside /app 
  #!/bin/bash

  cd app || exit 1




  # App folders
  mkdir -p app
  [ -d z_controllers ] && mv z_controllers app/Controllers
  [ -d z_models ]      && mv z_models      app/Models
  [ -d z_views ]       && mv z_views       app/Views
  [ -d z_database ]    && mv z_database    app/Database
  [ -d routes ]        && mv routes        app/Routes




  # package.json
  if grep -q 'z_database/import.php' package.json; then
      sed -i 's#z_database/import.php#app/Database/import.php#' package.json
  fi


  # Update the root index.php
  if grep -q '\$z_framework[[:space:]]*->[[:space:]]*execute' index.php; then
      sed -i -E 's/\$z_framework[[:space:]]*->[[:space:]]*execute[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*\)[[:space:]]*;/\$z_framework->handleRequest();/g' index.php
  fi




  # Webroot
  mkdir -p webroot




  # .htaccess
  [ -f webroot/.htaccess ] && rm webroot/.htaccess
  touch webroot/.htaccess
  cat > webroot/.htaccess << 'EOF'
  RewriteEngine On 
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f 
  RewriteRule . index.php [L,QSA]
  EOF

  [ -f .htaccess ] && rm .htaccess




  # Move all public files to webroot by excluding certain files and folders
  EXCLUDE=(
    app
    webroot
    z_framework _framework
    .vscode
    node_modules
    package.json package-lock.json
    composer.json composer.lock composer.local.json
    .dockerignore Dockerfile
    .htaccess 
    .z_framework
    index.php
    .drone.yml
    .gitignore .git
    z_config
    vendor
    Validator helper
    packaging
    tests
    libs
    TODO
    sql.log
    README.md
    LICENSE
    src source
    examples example
  )


  for item in *; do
    if [[ " ${EXCLUDE[*]} " =~ " $item " ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    mv -v "$item" "webroot"
  done




  # Create index.php in webroot
  [ -f webroot/index.php ] && rm webroot/index.php
  touch webroot/index.php

  cat > webroot/index.php << 'EOF'
  <?php

      // -----------------------------
      // Do not change this file as it is the entrypoint for web requests.
      // -----------------------------

      chdir(__DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . '..' . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR);

      // Try multiple locations for the entry scripts
      $entryScripts = [
          "index.php",
          "zubzet.php",
          "zubzet",
      ];

      $entryScriptFound = false;

      foreach($entryScripts as $entryScript) {
          if(!file_exists($entryScript)) break;

          require_once $entryScript;
          $entryScriptFound = true;
      }

      // If no entry script is found, return a 500 error
      if(!$entryScriptFound) {
          http_response_code(500);
          echo "No entry script found.";
          exit(1);
      }

  ?>
EOF

echo "Done."

docs.title: Migrating version 0.9 to 0.10
docs.text:
The update system has been changed. Before upgrading to 0.11.x, please run the legacy updater one last time using the Admin Dashboard or by running the command php z_framework/updater.php in the root directory of your project.

Make sure that you have pulled the latest version of 0.10.x before running the legacy updater.

docs.title: Repository URL
docs.text:
The repository URL has changed. ZubZet now made it to Github! To update your submodule, run the following command in the z_framework folder.

SSH

Update to the new repo URL using SSH: 

git submodule set-url z_framework ssh://git@github.com:zubzet/framework.git

HTTPS

Update to the new repo URL using HTTPS: 

git submodule set-url z_framework https://github.com/zubzet/framework.git

Be sure to checkout to 0.11.0 afterwards! 

cd z_framework
git checkout 0.11.0

docs.title: Mail Security
docs.text:
There is a new config setting called mail_security, which allows setting the transport security when sending mails. Until now, it has always been tls, which is why tls is the default value for this setting. No update to the configuration file i needed. If you i.e. use a local mailer, which requires a plain connection, you may set this setting to false. The following steps are recommended to migrate local test setup, which use environment variables to overwrite settings:

  1. Set the value mail_security in the configuration file to tls.
  2. Set the environment variable CONFIG_MAIL_SECURITY to "false". (Include the ")

This way a production deployment does not need to overwrite this value, while allowing for local plain connections.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• New Features
  • Upgrade Steps

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text: ZubZet now includes significantly enhanced access control and permission capabilities. This update introduces improved developer ergonomics, support for user-based permissions, and a more flexible and extensible authorization workflow.

docs.title: Migration System
docs.text: The migration system has been implemented. It provides developers with a structured and consistent way to manage database migrations, seed data, and environment-specific execution.

docs.title: Global Helper Functions
docs.text: To simplify development and reduce boilerplate, a set of global helper functions is now available. These helpers provide more convenient access to application objects and services.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: ZubZet can now be managed more efficiently through console commands. This allows for improved automation, maintenance, and development workflows.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text: Follow these steps to upgrade your project to version 1.1.0. These changes ensure compatibility with the new migration architecture and automated deployment workflow.

docs.title: 1. Automated Migration (Recommended)
docs.text:
You can automate most of these steps using the ZubZet Version Migrator.

  1. Get the tool: it lives in the migrator/ folder of the zubzet/framework repository; run composer install there
  2. Run the upgrade command in your terminal: 
    php application.php upgrade {PATH_TO_YOUR_PROJECT} {YOUR_CURRENT_VERSION} 1.1.0

docs.title: 2.1 Update Database Settings (z_settings.ini)
docs.text:
Add two new keys to your configuration. These elevated credentials are used specifically for schema modifications.

  • dbusername_elevated
  • dbpassword_elevated

If left empty, the system falls back to the default database user.

docs.title: 2.2 Update package.json
docs.text:
• Seed Command: Change "php app/Database/import.php" to "php zubzet db:seed" in your seed script.
  • Start Script: Remove the && npm run seed suffix from your start script.

docs.title: 2.3 Docker Integration (docker-compose-base.yml)
docs.text:
Update your Docker configuration to include the new migration service and dependency checks.

Add the migration service:

services:
  migration:
    <<: *built-application-image
    command: php zubzet db:migrate
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      database:
        condition: service_healthy

Update x-built-application-image dependencies: Add the following to the depends_on section of your application image:

depends_on:
  migration:
    condition: service_completed_successfully

docs.title: 3.1 Filename Convention Check
docs.text:
Every migration file in app/Database/migrations must follow the new format: YYYY-MM-DD_{INDEX}_{NAME}.{php/sql}

Review all existing files. If they do not match this pattern, rename them accordingly, or the migration system will abort.

docs.title: 3.2 Remove Legacy Framework Migrations
docs.text:
Delete migrations that target internal z_ tables (e.g., z_user, z_role, z_file).

  • Standard files to remove: 2021-02-04_zubzet.sql, 2025-11-06_user_permissions.

Ensure no local migrations modify these tables: z_email_verify, z_file, z_interaction_log, z_interaction_log_category, z_language, z_logintoken, z_logintry, z_login_too_many_tries, z_password_reset, z_role, z_role_permission, z_uniqueref, z_user, z_user_role, z_user_permission.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• New Features
  • Bugfixes
  • Breaking Changes
  • Upgrade Steps

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: ZubZet now includes a built-in logging system powered by Monolog. It supports two backends — database and stream — and is enabled by default. The framework automatically records system events such as logins, page views, and REST errors.

docs.title: Maintenance System
docs.text: ZubZet now ships with a built-in maintenance system that lets you put your application into maintenance mode. While active, incoming requests are intercepted and visitors see a dedicated maintenance page instead of the regular site. This makes it easy to perform deployments, database migrations, or other administrative work without risking inconsistent state for users.

docs.title: info:startup command
docs.text: A new info:startup console command gives you a quick overview of your runtime environment. It prints information such as your PHP version, the installed ZubZet version, the configured port, the active environment, and other relevant details.

docs.title: Static Argument Support for Routes, Middlewares and Afterwares
docs.text: Routes, middlewares, and afterwares now accept static arguments directly in their definition. You can now pass them inline when declaring a route, which keeps route definitions self-contained and easier to read. This is particularly useful for reusable middlewares that need slightly different parameters on different routes.

docs.title: Coverage Report
docs.text: You can now collect a code coverage report at runtime. Run testing:coverage:start to begin recording, execute the code paths you want to measure (through tests, manual requests, or any other means), and then run testing:coverage:stop to finish the session. A full coverage report is generated for you, making it easy to see which parts of your application are exercised and which still need test coverage.

docs.title: $res->json()
docs.text: The response object now exposes a dedicated $res->json() helper for sending JSON responses. It takes care of encoding the payload and returning the response in one concise call.

docs.title: Slow Query and Slow Request Logging
docs.text: The logging system now automatically records slow database queries and slow requests. When a query or request exceeds the configured threshold, it is written to the log along with timing information, making it much easier to spot performance bottlenecks in production. You no longer need to instrument your code by hand to find the parts of your application that are dragging down response times.

docs.title: PHP Debug Bar
docs.text: A PHP Debug Bar has been integrated into the framework and is available in the test environment. It surfaces information about the current request, executed database queries, rendered templates, log records with full context, and other runtime details directly in the browser. See the Debug Bar documentation for configuration, internal-query filtering, and how to mark your own models as internal.

docs.title: Whoops Error Page
docs.text: The Whoops error page has been added for the test environment. Instead of a plain error message, unhandled exceptions are now rendered with full stack traces, source code snippets, and request context. This provides a significantly richer debugging experience and helps you pinpoint the cause of errors much faster during development.

docs.title: Auto Start and Stop
docs.text: ZubZet projects now start and stop automatically when you open or close them in your editor. You no longer need to manually run a start command every time you switch projects — the framework detects the context and brings the project up or tears it down on its own. This streamlines the development workflow, especially when working on multiple ZubZet projects at once.

docs.title: Asset Proxy
docs.text: Assets are no longer served directly as static files. Instead, an asset proxy now sits in front of the file delivery and handles the requests, which opens the door to on-the-fly processing, access control, and caching strategies. Existing asset URLs continue to work as before, so this change is transparent for applications that simply serve files.

docs.title: Include / Exclude Environments in Seed Command
docs.text: The seed command now accepts explicit include and exclude filters for environments. You can target a specific environment with its seeds, or exclude certain environments from a broader seed run. This makes it much easier to maintain separate seed data sets for development, testing, and production without accidentally mixing them up.

docs.title: PHP 8.5 Support
docs.text: ZubZet now officially supports PHP 8.5. The framework has been tested against the latest PHP release and runs out of the box on 8.5, so you can take advantage of the newest language features and runtime improvements. Older supported PHP versions continue to work as before, allowing you to upgrade on your own schedule.

docs.title: Native Argon2id Password Hashing
docs.text: Password storage now uses PHP's native Argon2id, the algorithm recommended by the current OWASP Password Storage guidance, in place of the previous SHA-512 based scheme. Argon2id is memory hard and purpose built for password storage, and the native PHP functions embed the algorithm, cost, and salt in every stored value. Existing passwords are safe and keep working: they are upgraded to Argon2id automatically the next time their owner logs in, so adopting the modern format requires no password reset. See the new Password Handling documentation for the full picture, including the verify and hash API and how to add users.

docs.title: Missing Migration Folder
docs.text: Running migrations no longer fails when the migration folder does not exist. Instead of raising an error, the framework now creates the folder automatically and continues as expected. This removes a common friction point when setting up a fresh project or working in a freshly cloned checkout.

docs.title: Larger File Size Support
docs.text: The size column of the z_file table has been changed from a regular integer to a BIGINT. This raises the supported file size well beyond the previous ~2 GB limit and allows ZubZet to correctly handle very large uploads and stored files. Applications that deal with video, archives, or other large binary assets will benefit from this change immediately.

docs.title: Removed: Log category methods on models
docs.text:
The following methods have been removed from the base model class:

  • getLogCategoryIdByName()
  • logAction()
  • logActionByCategory()

If your application calls any of these methods, replace them with the new logger() helper. See the Logging documentation for usage.

docs.title: Removed: z_interaction_log_category table
docs.text: The z_interaction_log_category table has been dropped entirely. The categoryId column has also been removed from z_interaction_log.

docs.title: Removed: Log viewer in Admin Panel
docs.text: The log viewer previously available in the Admin Panel has been removed.

docs.title: Removed: Global request variables
docs.text: The PHP superglobals ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE, etc.) are no longer populated or used by the framework for accessing request data. All request input must now be read through the request object, for example via $req->input. This keeps request handling consistent, testable, and decoupled from PHP's global state — but it does mean that any code still relying on the superglobals needs to be migrated to the request API.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text: Follow these steps to upgrade your project to v1.2.0.

docs.title: 1. Automated migration (recommended)
docs.text:
Most of the changes below can be applied automatically with the ZubZet Version Migrator.

  1. Get the tool: it lives in the migrator/ folder of the zubzet/framework repository; run composer install there
  2. Preview the changes with a dry run, then apply them:
php application.php upgrade {PATH_TO_YOUR_PROJECT} 1.1.0 1.2.0 --dry
php application.php upgrade {PATH_TO_YOUR_PROJECT} 1.1.0 1.2.0

The migrator bumps the framework dependency, adds the new z_settings.ini keys (logging, maintenance mode, debug bar, editor), updates .gitignore and package.json, rewrites direct superglobal and php://input access to the request API, and installs the VS Code tasks. Review each prompted change before accepting it.

After the migrator finishes, apply the database changes (step 4) and rebuild your stack.

docs.title: 2. Replace removed model methods
docs.text:
Search your application code for the removed methods and replace them with logger():

// Before
$this->logAction("Something happened");
$this->logActionByCategory("Something happened", "category");

// After
logger()->info("Something happened");

docs.title: 3. Move request input off superglobals
docs.text:
The framework no longer populates $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE, etc. Read input through the request object instead (the migrator automates this rewrite):

// Before
$_POST["email"];
file_get_contents("php://input");

// After
request()->input->POST["email"];
request()->input->body;

docs.title: 4. Apply the database migrations
docs.text:
The framework-bundled migrations below are applied automatically by the project's normal start/seed flow (npm run start, which runs db:seed → migrations then seed) or directly with:

docker exec application php index.php db:migrate

New since v1.1.0:

Migration Change 2026-03-27_session-handling.sql Adds z_logintoken.extended_seconds and active. Corrects a file misdated 2027-03-27 in 1.1.0 — its ALTER TABLE is not re-runnable. 2026-04-02_deprecate_interactionlog.sql Drops z_interaction_log_category and z_interaction_log.categoryId. 2026-04-27_organization.sql Creates z_organization; adds z_user.organizationId. 2026-05-04_organization_role.sql Adds z_organization.groupId for organization-level roles; its ALTER TABLE is not re-runnable.

If you manage schema by hand, the equivalent statements are idempotent (... IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS).

docs.title: 5. Configure logging (optional)
docs.text:
Logging is enabled by default with the database backend. The migrator writes the level info into z_settings.ini (without a logger_level key the framework logs at notice). To adjust the behavior, set the relevant keys in z_config/z_settings.ini:

logger_enabled = true
logger_type = database
logger_level = info

To disable logging entirely:

logger_enabled = false

See the Logging documentation for all available options.

docs.title: 4. Adopt native password hashing
docs.text:
The schema migration runs automatically when the framework updates. It adds a password_scheme and a last_password_rehash_at column to z_user and marks every existing password row as legacy. No action is required for accounts to keep working: they verify through the legacy path and upgrade themselves to Argon2id on the next successful login.

Rehash on login only reaches accounts that log in. To bring accounts that have not logged in yet onto Argon2id as well, run the onion migration once. It is idempotent and safe to re run:

php index.php auth:migrate-hashing

See the Password Handling documentation for the verify and hash API, the scheme model, and how to add users.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• New Features
  • Requirements
  • Breaking Changes
  • Upgrade Steps

docs.title: Katana Blade render engine
docs.text: Views are now rendered with Katana, a standalone implementation of the Blade templating language. This brings real template inheritance, reusable <x-...> components, shared partials and the full set of Blade directives (@if, @foreach, @forelse, @include, and more) to your views. See the rewritten Views documentation for what is now possible.

docs.title: UUIDs on authentication objects
docs.text:
Users, roles, groups, organizations, sessions and api keys (and the z_file table) carry a UUID next to their numeric ID. It is the identifier meant to leave the application - URLs, REST payloads, anything handed to a third party - because it does not reveal how many records exist and cannot be guessed by counting up. The numeric ID stays the internal key.

Every object that can be retrieved by ID can also be retrieved by UUID, and every object exposes its own:

$user = User::byUuid($uuid);
$roles = Role::byUuids(...$uuids);

user()->uuid;
$user->uuid();
$organization->uuid();

For a session or an api key the UUID is the only identifier safe to publish - the token authenticates whoever presents it, so it belongs in a cookie or an Authorization header and nowhere else. Use the UUID to address a session in a "your active sessions" list:

$session = Session::byUuid($uuid); // scoped like byId(): never returns an api key
$key = APIKey::byUuid($uuid);

See Access Control for the full API.

docs.title: Organization self-management
docs.text:
Members can manage their own organization in the Z-Admin panel at /z/organization: rename it (z.organization.rename), invite existing accounts by link (z.organization.invite) and hand out roles that are released to organizations (z.organization.roles). The sidebar entry and the dashboard card show up with z.organization.manage. A role is released with the new Organizations may assign this role to their members checkbox on its page under Roles. Nothing is released after the upgrade, so organizations can only hand out roles once you tick it.

See Organization Management.

docs.title: Two factor authentication
docs.text:
Accounts can protect their logins with a time based one time password from an authenticator app. Users set it up on their profile page. A login of an account with two factor then asks for the code in a modal before the session starts, and $req->requireFreshTwoFactor() guards a single action behind a check within two_factor_freshness_seconds (defaults to 900).

The modal ships with <x-zubzet::body/>. A layout that leaves out the body essentials cannot finish a two factor login until it renders <x-zubzet::authentication.two-factor/> itself.

See Two Factor Authentication.

docs.title: Profile page
docs.text:
Every logged in account has a profile page at /z/profile: password change, two factor, sessions and api keys. It is built from the zubzet::account.* components, which can be placed on any page. See Profile.

A password change ends every login of the account but no longer its api keys, and neither does $user->clearSessions(). Revoke keys through APIKey::byUser() where a password change used to end them.

docs.title: MariaDB 11.7 or newer
docs.text:
v1.3.0 raises the minimum database server to MariaDB 11.7. Older servers are no longer supported.

ZubZet targets MariaDB, not MySQL: the framework-bundled migrations use MariaDB-only syntax (ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), which MySQL rejects. The development stack and the e2e suite run MariaDB 11.8.

Check what your server runs:

SELECT VERSION();

docs.title: Views are now Blade templates
docs.text:
The old view format, a PHP file returning head and body closures, has been replaced by Blade .blade.php templates. The change is mechanical and the migrator applies it for you:

  • A view's body closure becomes @section("content").
  • A view's head closure becomes @section("head").
  • Every view starts with @extends($layout), so the view plugs into the layout the controller chose.
  • Layouts drop their $body($opt) / $head($opt) calls in favor of @yield("content") / @yield("head"), and the framework essentials become the <x-zubzet::head :opt="$opt"/> and <x-zubzet::body :opt="$opt"/> components.

Before:

<?php return ["body" => function($opt) { ?>
    <h1><?= $opt["title"] ?></h1>
<?php }]; ?>

After:

@extends($layout)

@section("content")
    <h1>{{ $opt["title"] }}</h1>
@endsection

Plain PHP still works inside a .blade.php file, so raw <?php ?> blocks in your views keep running unchanged. See the Views documentation for the full picture.

docs.title: Requests from other sites are rejected
docs.text: Every request that can change state (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, ...) is checked for CSRF by the headers the browser sets. A form or fetch() call from a site that is not allowed is answered with 403 until its origin is listed. GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are not checked, so links, redirects and callbacks keep working. See step 7.

docs.title: Upgrade Steps
docs.text: Follow these steps to upgrade your project to v1.3.0.

docs.title: 1. Upgrade the database server first
docs.text:
Bring the server to 11.7 or newer before applying the migrations of this release. With the Docker stack, bump the mariadb image in packaging/docker/docker-compose-base.yml and recreate the container:

image: mariadb:11.8

docs.title: 2. Automated migration (recommended)
docs.text:
The ZubZet Version Migrator converts every view and layout in your project automatically.

  1. Get the tool: it lives in the migrator/ folder of the zubzet/framework repository; run composer install there
  2. Preview the changes with a dry run, then apply them:
php application.php upgrade {PATH_TO_YOUR_PROJECT} 1.2.0 1.3.0 --dry
php application.php upgrade {PATH_TO_YOUR_PROJECT} 1.2.0 1.3.0

The migrator bumps the framework dependency, adds the new z_settings.ini keys and rewrites every return [...] view and layout to Blade (.blade.php), including the section, @extends and essentials-component changes above. It also removes app-local copies of Z.js, since the framework serves the current one itself, and adds a .htaccess to webroot/uploads/ (see step 11). Review each prompted change before accepting it.

docs.title: 3. Review your migrated views
docs.text: The conversion is output preserving, but it is worth skimming the result. Views that already used raw <?php ?> keep it verbatim, and anything the framework could not classify is left as raw PHP rather than guessed at. Once you are comfortable with Blade, you can gradually adopt directives like @foreach or components where they make a template clearer. The Views documentation covers what is available.

docs.title: 4. Apply the database migrations
docs.text:
The framework-bundled migrations are applied by the project's normal start/seed flow (npm run start, which runs db:seed → migrations then seed) or directly with:

docker exec application php index.php db:migrate

New since v1.2.0:

Migration Change 2026-09-02_user_locale_bcp_47.sql Adds the nullable z_user.locale_bcp_47, the user's preferred locale. 2026-09-07_session-api-key.sql Adds z_logintoken.name, is_permanent and is_apikey. 2026-09-08_session-device-and-ip.sql Adds z_logintoken.device, reason, ip_creation and ip_last. 2026-09-08_uuid.sql Adds the NOT NULL, indexed uuid column (native UUID type) to z_user, z_role, z_organization, z_logintoken and z_file. 2026-09-09_session-expires-at.sql Adds the nullable z_logintoken.expires_at (TIMESTAMP), the fixed expiry that overrides the computed session lifetime. 2026-09-17_session-last-used-and-token-index.sql Adds the nullable z_logintoken.last_used (TIMESTAMP). 2026-09-21_two-factor-challenge.sql Creates z_two_factor_challenge for the login's two factor step, and adds z_logintoken.last_two_factor, z_user.two_factor_secret and z_user.two_factor_confirmed_at. 2026-09-21_2_session-two-factor-tries.sql Adds z_logintoken.remaining_two_factor_tries (defaults to 5). 2026-09-23_group-org-assignable.sql Adds z_role.is_org_assignable (TINYINT(1), default 0), which releases a role or group to organizations. 2026-09-23_organization-invite.sql Creates z_organization_invite, the invitation links of organizations. 2026-10-02_session-token-index.sql Adds a unique index on z_logintoken.token, so the session lookup no longer scans the table. 2026-11-09_organization-permissions.sql Creates z_organization_permission and z_organization_role, which every permission check reads.

If you manage schema by hand, the equivalent statements are idempotent (... IF NOT EXISTS).

docs.title: 5. Check code that builds URLs from the root directory
docs.text:
v1.3.0 fixes how a non-empty rootDirectory is handled. With an empty rootDirectory (the default, and what the Docker stack sets through CONFIG_ROOTDIRECTORY: "") nothing changes. Below a root directory such as sub:

Value v1.2.0 v1.3.0 $opt["root"], $req->getRootFolder(), Z.Request.rootPath /sub /sub/ $opt["absRoot"], $opt["application_root"], $req->getRoot(), config("root"), Z.Request.absRoot, Z.Request.rootHost https://example.com/sub https://example.com/sub/ Route::get("/hello") on /sub/hello no match (compared against the full path) matches getUrlParts() of /sub/a/b with rootDirectory = sub/ ["b"] (the slash counted as a segment) ["a", "b"] $res->reroute(["a", "b"]) 404 (the root directory was missing from the rerouted path) runs a/b

The only code that needs a change is code that adds its own slash after the root. The router answers the resulting /sub//login like /sub/login, so such links keep working until cleaned up:

// before: /sub//login after the upgrade
$opt["root"] . "/login"
// after
$opt["root"] . "login"

Search your project for a slash right after any of the values in the first two rows (root"] . "/, root ?>/, {{ $opt["root"] }}/, rootPath + "/", ...) and for paths with a leading slash handed to helpers that prepend the root themselves (rerouteUrl("/, Z.Request.root("/). Routes, reroute() calls and getUrlParts() need no change as long as they are written relative to the root directory, which is the only form that worked before.

A cookie path taken from getRootFolder() now ends with a slash as well, so the browser no longer sends that cookie on the bare /sub. Pass rtrim($req->getRootFolder(), "/") ?: "/" instead, as the framework does for its maintenance cookie.

docs.title: What was checked
docs.text:
Before the release, the change was checked against eleven existing applications, built on framework versions from v0.11 to v1.3.0-alpha, by reading their code against the old and the new behaviour. Each application was checked for:

  • every concatenation of $opt["root"], $opt["absRoot"], getRoot(), getRootFolder(), config("root") and Z.Request.rootPath/rootHost/absRoot in controllers, models, views, mail views and JavaScript
  • Route:: definitions and groups, reroute(), rerouteUrl(), getUrlParts() and direct REQUEST_URI access
  • .htaccess (RewriteBase), maintenance and login cookie paths, and debug bar usage
  • overrides of email_password_reset and translation keys under email.*
  • the effective rootDirectory per environment: the INI value, the Docker setup and the production and staging deployments

Result:

Setup found Applications Outcome Deployed with CONFIG_ROOTDIRECTORY: "" (every production, staging and Docker environment) 11 Identical values, routes and reroutes INI rootDirectory without a trailing slash (sub, also with spaces) 5 Links like /sublogin and routes below the root are fixed INI rootDirectory with a trailing slash (sub/) on v1.2 2 The autorouter no longer strips the controller, links are fixed INI rootDirectory with a trailing slash (sub/) on v0.11 to v1.0 2 Identical values, those versions already used the value verbatim INI rootDirectory empty 2 Identical values A slash added after the root (root . "/path") 0 Would keep working with a doubled slash, the change shown above removes it Route:: paths that include the root directory 0 Would need the root directory removed

Root directories with spaces (My App) behave the same: the router decodes the request path before stripping the root directory, and getUrlParts() counts the encoded segment as one, so both agree on real requests and on reroutes.

The e2e suite serves the application below /sub as well and covers this in tests/cypress/e2e/core/root-directory.cy.js (links, assets and the debug bar, Route:: definitions, reroutes, a doubled slash after the root, the maintenance cookie, the password reset mail) and tests/cypress/e2e/core/request.cy.js (getUrlParts() with one, two and slash-wrapped segments, and a doubled slash after them).

docs.title: 6. Send the login warning yourself if you relied on it
docs.text:
Too many failed logins no longer send the "Security alert" email to the account owner; the login is still blocked and logged as ACCOUNT_LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED. The email_too_many_logins view, the z_login_too_many_tries table and the z_loginModel helpers around it stay, so no migration is needed, but the framework no longer calls them. To keep the warning, send it when checkLoginTries() returns false:

if(!$user->checkLoginTries()) {
    $res->sendEmailToUser($user->id(), "Security alert", "email_too_many_logins.php", [
        "date" => date("Y-m-d H:i:s"),
        "ip" => $req->ip(),
    ]);
}

$req->ip() returns the first value that is set out of HTTP_CLIENT_IP, HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR and REMOTE_ADDR, so REMOTE_ADDR, the only address the client cannot choose, is used only when neither header is present. The framework does not strip these headers and does not know a list of trusted proxies, so any client can send them and the address is spoofable. X-Forwarded-For may also hold a comma separated chain. The same value ends up in ip_creation of sessions and two factor challenges and in ip_last of sessions. The view prints it unescaped. Validate it with filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP) before it goes into the mail, otherwise an attacker can put HTML into a security mail to the account owner, and do not use it as proof of where a login came from unless your proxy overwrites both headers. checkLoginTries() returns false on every blocked attempt, so the example sends one mail per attempt. Throttle it, the removed code sent at most one mail per 10 minutes.

docs.title: 7. Allow the sites that send requests to your application
docs.text:
Requests from other sites are answered with 403

Every request but GET, HEAD and OPTIONS is now checked against Cross-Site Request Forgery. A form post or fetch() call that a page of another site starts is rejected with 403 unless that site is allowed. Check every endpoint that is called from outside before you deploy, and every action that changes state on a GET.

The check judges a request by the headers the browser sets (Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin), with no token, cookie or form field, so forms, Z.Forms, Z.Request and your own fetch() calls keep working unchanged. A request with neither header (curl, servers, webhooks) passes, and one with an Origin but no Sec-Fetch-Site (old browsers, plain http://) only meets csrf_blocked_origins. A checked request whose page hides its Origin (no-referrer, a sandboxed iframe) passes only from the application's own origin. What is rejected now:

  • Form posts from other sites, among them OAuth and SAML callbacks by form_post and payment returns that post back.
  • Pages of your own on other hosts or subdomains that post to the application.
  • fetch() calls from other origins that change state; their CORS preflight passes.

Links, redirects, embedded images and every other GET, HEAD or OPTIONS pass. An action that changes state on a GET is therefore unprotected: move it to a POST, or call $req->csrfBlockAdditionalMethod("GET", "HEAD") at its start, as the framework's logout does. See Protecting a normally safe method.

The migrator adds the three settings with their defaults, which accept requests from the application's own origin and from no page at all (a typed URL, a bookmark) only:

csrf_allow = same-origin
csrf_trusted_origins =
csrf_blocked_origins =

List the origins that legitimately send users or requests to the application in csrf_trusted_origins, for example the identity and the payment provider. Each entry is one origin exactly as the browser sends it, scheme://host[:port] without path, trailing slash or default port; wildcards are not supported. csrf_allow = any lets every site in, for an API without a cookie session. When every subdomain of your site is yours, csrf_allow = same-site accepts all of them, and csrf_blocked_origins takes single ones out again. See CSRF Protection for the decision, a table of common setups and the limits.

docs.title: 8. Check what depends on the session cookie
docs.text:
The z_login_token session cookie and the maintenance bypass cookie now carry SameSite=Lax, and Secure whenever the host setting starts with https://. This can break three things:

  • A deployment whose host says https:// but is served over plain HTTP loses its logins until host matches the real scheme.
  • A cross-site POST that returns to the application (OIDC form_post, SAML, payment returns) arrives without the session cookie.
  • A request from a cross-site iframe has no session cookie either.

docs.title: 9. Set encryption_key if you use secrets
docs.text:
encryptSecret() and decryptSecret() need the encryption_key setting, at least 32 bytes. Set it via CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY and keep an empty encryption_key = line in z_settings.ini, because environment variables only override settings that exist there. Values encrypted with a key cannot be recovered once it is changed or lost.

See Secrets.

docs.title: 10. If requests fail with "Illegal mix of collations"
docs.text:
Framework tables are now created as utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci. Existing installations are not converted, because converting rewrites every table. If tables created under different server defaults make queries fail with Illegal mix of collations, convert the framework tables once, ideally in a maintenance window:

docker exec application php index.php repair:database-collation

Add --include-app-tables to convert the application tables too and to set the database default.

See Console Commands.

docs.title: 11. Protect other upload folders in the webroot
docs.text:
Files in webroot/uploads/ are only served now, never run through PHP: the migrator adds a .htaccess there. Without it, an upload field that accepts the php extension lets anyone run code by opening the uploaded file. If uploadFolder or an upload() call points to another folder in the webroot, put the same .htaccess there:

<Files "*">
    SetHandler None
</Files>

docs.title: 13. Check code that reads session tokens
docs.text: Newly issued session and api key tokens are zub-sha256- plus 64 hex characters (75 in total) and are stored hashed. For such a token token() returns the plain value only on a session created by add() or byToken(); on one loaded by any other retriever it is null, and storedToken() returns the stored value. Sessions and api keys issued before the upgrade stay valid and keep returning their token from every retriever, with a deprecation notice that showErrors = 2 promotes to an exception, so development setups see it right away. Widen anything that validates a token by its length, and compare z_logintoken.token in your own SQL against storedToken() or LoginToken::hash($token).

docs.title: Sending an email
docs.text:
To send an email there are two methods in response called sendEmail() and sendEmailToUser().

$subject can be an array keyed by language (keys are lowercased) to serve subjects for multiple languages. The entry of $lang is used, falling back to en, so an en entry is required. $document is the path to a view. Any view can be used as a mail. But it is wise to create extra ones, because script stuff won't work. Be careful not to leak data that only the requested account has access to. $opt are parameters to pass into the view. There, $opt["overwrite_lang"] holds the lowercased $lang (null becomes en), $opt["application_root"] the host plus root folder for absolute links, and $opt["user"] the user of the current request, not the recipient.

This method uses render() internally. render() does not throw for a missing $document or layout: it catches the view-not-found error and renders the framework's 500 view in layout/min_layout instead, so the mail is still sent with the error page as its body. Check the view name, especially for views you ship yourself.

sendEmail() sends synchronously to a single recipient (no CC, BCC, reply-to, queue or retry) and returns true after sending. The body goes out as UTF-8 HTML with a plain-text alternative made by stripping its tags. If PHPMailer fails (SMTP unreachable, rejected login), it echoes Message could not be sent. Mailer Error: ... into the response output and returns false; nothing is logged. The default $layout is email, which resolves to layout/email_layout (mail, mail_layout and layout/mail_layout.php all name the same layout); the framework only ships layout/mail_layout, so create email_layout yourself or pass another layout.

docs.title: Bundled mail views
docs.text:
The framework ships three mail views, each a .blade.php file that a view of the same name in your z_views directory replaces:

  • email_verify is sent when someone signs up or asks for a new verification link. It expects the option url. The subject is <pageName> - Sign Up and the pageName setting must exist in the booter settings: the framework reads it with getBooterSettings("pageName", ""), whose second argument is $useDefault, and the empty string counts as false, so a missing key throws an InvalidArgumentException instead of falling back to an empty prefix.
  • email_password_reset is sent by the forgot-password flow. It expects the option reset_link.
  • email_too_many_logins expects the options date and ip. $req->ip() can be spoofed with a request header and the view prints it unescaped, validate it first. The framework no longer sends it itself, see Send the login warning yourself.

A mail view you add yourself should not reuse these names unless it is meant to replace the bundled one. All three are written in Blade and extend $layout.

For this feature to work a mail address needs to be configured in the booter settings and a SMTP service needs to be available. PHP need to be setup correctly too.

Example code for sending a mail: 

public function action_register(Request $req, Response $res) {
    if($req->isAction("register")) {
        $email = $req->getPost("email");
        $password = $req->getPost("password");

        $response = $req->getModel("Employee")->register($email, $password);

        if(!$response) {
            return $res->error();
        }

        $res->sendEmail(
            $email          ,                                         // Target address
            ["en" => "Welcome Mail", "de" => "Willkommens Mail"],     // Subject
            "email_welcome",                                         // Path to the email view
            "en",                                                     // Language used in the email
            [
                "email" => $email
            ],                                                        // Options
            "employee/mail_layout"                                    // Layout to use
        );
    }
}

docs.title: Example Layout
docs.text:
<html>
    <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8"/>
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"/>
        @yield("head")
    </head>
    <body>
        Welcome <?= $opt["email"] ?>!
        @yield("content")
    </body>
</html>

docs.title: Send to registered users
docs.text:
sendEmailToUser() sends a mail to an user identified by its user id. The mail address and language are fetched from the database, so less information is needed; if the z_language row of z_user.languageId has no value, the anonymous_language setting (no default) is used, and en if that is unset too. It returns the result of sendEmail(), and its default layout is the bundled layout/mail_layout, which only prints the view's content. It throws an Exception if the user does not exist or has no email address.

Exmaple: 

$res->sendEmailToUser(
    1,                                                             // User ID
    ["en" => "New cooking recipes!", "de" => "Neue Kochrezepte!"], // Subject
    "email_recipes",                                              // Path to the mail view
    ["r1" => "Cake", "r2" => "Cookies!!!"],                        // Options
    "layout/email_layout"                                         // Layout to use
);

docs.title: Login: Login as another user
docs.text:
When logging in, the client exchanges it's identifier and password for a authentication token and logs in using this token from that point on. $res->loginAs allows you to login a current client as another user by their z_user.`id`.

The authentication token will track the exec user though. using this data, you'll always know who was logged in as who. You can also set an exec_user yourself, using the second argument of loginAs (default: the logged in user itself). You are also able to login as another user using the very same panel.

Example: 

$res->loginAs(1, 2); //Logs the requesting session in as user 1 and marks the real user as 2.

loginAs is a plain session issuer and has no guards: it performs no permission check (the caller decides who may use it), does not invalidate the user's other sessions (concurrent sessions are allowed) and does not change user() of the current request. The new login applies from the next request on, when the client sends the cookie. $userId is typed int, so a non-numeric string (for example from a URL) throws a TypeError. It logs USER_LOGGED_IN, or USER_LOGGED_IN_ANOTHER when $user_exec differs from $userId.

$res->logout() invalidates only the current session and logs USER_LOGGED_OUT. During a login as another user it then calls loginAs() for the exec user, which issues a fresh token, otherwise it deletes the cookie, and it always ends with a redirect to the root, also for a client that is not logged in.

docs.title: Naming a session and recording why it exists
docs.text:
Every session records the request that created it on its own: device holds the user agent and ip_creation the address. The two optional arguments are what you choose yourself - a $name for the label a "your active sessions" list shows, and a $reason for why the session exists, which is what makes an impersonation traceable afterwards:

$res->loginAs(1, 2, "Support session", "Ticket #4711"); //Names the session and records why it was opened

Both values are read back through Session::byUser().

docs.title: The session cookie
docs.text:
loginAs sends the token to the client as the z_login_token cookie, set through setFrameworkCookie (a wrapper around setCookie) with these attributes:

Attribute Value Expires time() + loginTimeoutSeconds (7 days when the setting is unset) Path / Domain .<domain> when login_scope_allow_subdomains is the string true, otherwise none (host-only). A second z_login_token delete header (on login and logout) is then sent for the domain in login_scope_allow_subdomains_delete_domainscope_name (to clean up cookies from before the switch) whenever that key exists, even empty, and an empty value deletes the host-only cookie just set Secure set when the host setting starts with https:// HttpOnly never set, because Z.js and the session watcher read the cookie in JavaScript SameSite Lax

docs.title: In the admin panel
docs.text:
The panel passes the current exec user on, so nested impersonation keeps the real identity, which checkSuperPermission() checks.

The "Login as" button on the user edit page asks for a reason before it sends you on. Leaving it empty or cancelling still logs you in - the session then records z-admin impersonation instead. Whatever is typed is cut to the 255 characters the column takes, so a long explanation shortens rather than failing.

docs.title: Organization Management
docs.text:
Members of an organization can manage it themselves in the Z-Admin panel at /z/organization. The page has up to four sections, each behind its own permission:

Section Permission Function Name z.organization.rename Rename the organization Invite a member z.organization.invite Create an invitation link Members z.organization.roles Give members roles and take them away again Open invitations z.organization.invite List and revoke invitations that are not accepted yet

A user who belongs to no organization sees a notice instead. The sidebar entry Organization (under Other) and the dashboard card show up with z.organization.manage. Without it the page is still reached through its direct link.

docs.title: Invitations
docs.text:
An invitation brings an existing account into the organization. No mail is sent: the page hands the inviting user a link to pass on.

  • Only an active account that belongs to no organization can be invited. Every other address gets the same message, so the form does not reveal which case applies.
  • An address holds one open invitation per organization at a time.
  • An invitation is valid for 7 days. Expired invitations are no longer listed and no longer block a new one.
  • Revoking an invitation makes its link stop working right away.

The link leads to /z/organization/invitation/{token}. The invited person has to be logged in with the invited address. The page shows the organization, the address and when the invitation was created, and accepting it makes the account a member. The account also joins the organization's linked group, like on any $user->updateOrganization().

Unknown, expired and revoked links answer with a 404, and so does a link opened by another account or by a user who already belongs to an organization.

docs.title: Releasing Roles to Organizations
docs.text:
An organization can only hand out roles that are released to organizations. A role is released with the checkbox Organizations may assign this role to their members on its page under Roles, stored in z_role.is_org_assignable. The flag works for groups as well. The groups page cannot edit them yet, so a group is released in the database.

In the Members section every member gets a multi select of the released roles. Saving replaces the released roles the member holds with the selection. Roles that are not released stay untouched.

Warning

A released role hands its permissions to whoever an organization chooses. Only release roles meant for that, and keep the organization's own management permissions out of them unless its members may pass them on.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
The page is built from Blade components in the zubzet:: namespace, so an application can place them on its own pages. Each one checks its permission and renders nothing without it. They post to the framework's _zubzet/organization/* endpoints.

Component Props Permission <x-zubzet::organization.rename :name="$name"/> name: the current name z.organization.rename <x-zubzet::organization.invite/> - z.organization.invite <x-zubzet::organization.invites :invites="$invites"/> invites: invitation rows with an expires_at timestamp z.organization.invite <x-zubzet::organization.members :members="$members" :food="$roleFood"/> members: id, email and the held roles ids per member; food: the released roles as value/text pairs z.organization.roles <x-zubzet::organization.accept :token="$token"/> token: the invitation token logged in

The error messages come from Z.Lang in Z.js. Like its other texts, they can be overwritten in the layout after the layout essentials are embedded:

Key Default error_user_unavailable This user cannot be invited right now. error_already_invited This address already has an open invitation. error_invalid_token This invitation is invalid or has expired. error_already_in_organization You are already a member of an organization.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Every logged in account has a profile page in the Z-Admin panel at /z/profile. It is linked as Profile in the sidebar (under Other) and on the dashboard. The page only ever shows the requesting account, so it needs no permission.

Section Function Header Email, member since and the organization Security Change opens the password modal, and two factor is set up and turned off in place (two factor authentication) Sessions Every login of the account, with rename and revoke, and Clear all sessions API keys Create, rename and revoke api keys

docs.title: Password
docs.text: A new password ends every login of the account, the current browser included, so it has to sign in again. Api keys keep working, they are credentials of their own.

docs.title: Two Factor
docs.text:
Set up shows a QR code for the authenticator and the key to type in by hand. Two factor stays off until a code from the authenticator confirms that the secret arrived. Turning it off again asks for a current code. After two_factor_tries (defaults to 5) wrong codes the session is signed out. Clearing sessions, revoking a session or key and creating a key ask for a recent check first.

An owner who lost their authenticator cannot turn it off themselves. An admin with admin.user.edit can, with Disable two factor on the account's page under Edit User.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: Every login is listed with its name, the device, where it started and was last seen, and when it expires. The current one is marked This browser. A session can be renamed and revoked one by one, or all at once with Clear all sessions, which ends the current login as well. The last use is refreshed at most once per session_last_used_throttle_seconds (defaults to 60), so it reads as "around then".

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
A key is created with a name and a lifetime between 1 day and 1 year, or without an expiry. Its token is shown once, right after creating it, and cannot be read again. Keys are listed with the same details as sessions and can be renamed and revoked the same way.

The page is built from the account components, so the same pieces can be placed on a page of an application.

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text: The Z-Admin panel is a management panel you can open to edit/create users or roles/permissions.

docs.title: Using the Z-Admin panel
docs.text: The Z-Admin panel is a control panel all projects using the framework have. It is accessible with the z controller. For example, an URL like this: localhost/project/z or abcde.de/z or {yourdomain.tld}/{yourwebsite}/z. Only logged in accounts with the correct permissions are able to see this section; an anonymous visitor gets the login page instead.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
It has following categories:

Category Function Database Read-only table browser Maintenance Shows the state of the maintenance mode and sets the bypass cookie Groups List of permission groups Edit User Form to edit a user's email, roles, user permissions and organization; there is no password change Add User Form to add users; the email must be unique and valid (empty is stored as NULL), the password is required client-side only. The user is verified at once, gets no role and no mail; a password outside 3 to 1024 bytes is rejected only after the user was inserted, so that email stays taken Roles User permission managment Organization Organization management by its own members Profile Own password, two factor, sessions and api keys Organizations List of organizations plus a detail page to rename or delete one Add Organization Form to create an organization, optionally with a permission group

The dashboard cards are fixed and there is no widget API; to change the panel, override its views (administration/*, database/*, layout/z_admin_layout) with a view of the same name in your project (administration/groups gets the option groups, database/tables gets status with tables and approxRows). layout/z_admin_layout is the z controller's default layout and links {root}assets/img/favicon.png, which your app has to supply.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
To be able to use all functions, the following permissions are needed:

  • admin.panel (the dashboard at /z only)
  • admin.user.list (the user list at /z/edit_user)
  • admin.user.add (the Add User form and creating the user)
  • admin.user.edit (opening and saving a single user; admin.user.list is checked first on every /z/edit_user request)
  • admin.groups.list (the groups list)
  • admin.roles.list (the roles list; checked first on every /z/roles request, including create and delete)
  • admin.roles.create (the create action of /z/roles; the new role has an empty name and role names are unique, so rename it before creating the next)
  • admin.roles.edit (opening and saving a role; also required for delete)
  • admin.roles.delete (the delete action on a role)
  • admin.organizations.list (checked first on every /z/organizations request)
  • admin.organizations.create
  • admin.organizations.edit (opening and renaming an organization; also required for delete)
  • admin.organizations.delete (the delete action on an organization)
  • admin.maintenance
  • admin.database
  • admin.su (/z/login_as/{userId}, also used by the Login as button of the edit form)

admin.panel guards the dashboard at /z and nothing else. Every other action checks its own permission from the list above, so a user without admin.panel still reaches /z/roles, /z/edit_user and the rest by their direct URL, as long as they hold the permission of that action. The checks run against the effective user, so while logged in as another user that user needs the permission itself. The sidebar and the dashboard cards (icon only, in the sections Application, Users and Roles, and Other) only show the entries the user may open, except that Edit User is shown for admin.user.edit although its list needs admin.user.list.

Members manage their own organization with:

  • z.organization.manage: the sidebar entry and dashboard card
  • z.organization.invite
  • z.organization.roles
  • z.organization.rename

Profile is the exception: it only ever shows the requesting account, so every login reaches it without a permission.

The framework's own migrations create no admin role, user or permission. A project created with the install script ships a seed (app/Database/seed/accounts/0_permissions.sql) that adds the roles Admin (permission *.*) and User (permission dashboard), but no user account. Create a user, assign it the Admin role under Edit Users or in z_user_role, and for projects without that seed insert the grants into z_role_permission or z_user_permission yourself.

docs.title: Assigning roles
docs.text:
In order to assign any roles, you must go to Edit Users and select the user you want to give a role to. Hit the ‘+’ under the title ‘Roles’ and select the role the user should get. The list offers every active role, but a group only while the user already holds it. Groups follow the user's organization, so they are not handed out here. Be advised, each role gives special permissions, some give the user special powers, therefore please see the list above of what roles have which permissions.

After you set a role, you can either add more roles or save the user by clicking ‘submit’ at the bottom of the page. The user should now be able to use their role.

docs.title: Two factor
docs.text: An account with two factor shows Disable two factor on its page under Edit Users. It turns two factor off after a confirmation, so an owner who lost their authenticator can sign in with the password again and set it up anew. It needs admin.user.list and admin.user.edit.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text:
Add Organization creates an organization. Ticking Create a permission group also creates a group named after the organization ({name}_Group) and links it to the organization. Organization names may repeat, group names may not, so the checkbox reports an error when a group of that name already exists.

Organizations lists every active organization; opening one shows a form to rename it, the linked group, the users assigned to it, and a button to delete it. Renaming also renames the linked group when it is named {organization name}_Group, as created by the checkbox above, and fails with a uniqueness error when a group of the new name already exists. Deleting is a soft delete, the organization is set to inactive, its members are detached and the linked group is deactivated. The Delete button requires admin.organizations.delete.

docs.title: Assigning organizations
docs.text: Both Add User and Edit User carry an Organization select. Picking an entry assigns the user to that organization, the empty entry (---) unassigns them. The assignment goes through User::updateOrganization(), so the group of the previous organization is removed from the user and the group of the new one is added. An Edit User request without the organization field leaves the organization unchanged.

docs.title: Database browser
docs.text:
/z/database lists every table of the database with approximate row counts, /z/database/{table} shows its rows 20 per page (/page/{n}, five page numbers around the current one, a page beyond the last shows no rows), newest first by the last primary key column (the first column without one), and /z/database/{table}/csv (the Export button) exports up to 10000 rows. The CSV export does not neutralise spreadsheet formulas. It is a read-only viewer and exporter (no insert, edit, delete, filter or search) and needs the permission admin.database.

Only the columns named exactly password, pw, salt or hash are shown as ********, in the table view and in the CSV export. Every other column is shown in clear text, including z_logintoken.token, z_email_verify.token and z_password_reset.refId. Anyone holding admin.database can read these, and with them take over sessions or password resets, so grant it only to accounts you would trust with the database itself.
